background_notes.fact: For a jointly smooth u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m, the density e=|u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² is smooth and has time derivative 2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t. Its fixed-space time sections and fixed-time spatial sections are smooth on their respective domains.

background_notes.justification: Write each squared Euclidean norm as the finite sum of component squares. The one-variable product rule differentiates each square to twice its component times its time derivative. Joint smoothness gives equality ∂_t∂_{x_j}u=∂_{x_j}∂_t u componentwise, and restriction of smooth functions preserves smoothness. These are local calculus facts, including empty finite sums.

background_notes.justification: Each closed coordinate interval is Borel, so their finite product box is measurable.
